people.role: Head of Thối Tinh Môn since 1050, weapon forging from star iron; the only smith on the mountain who can hold the Rite of the Fallen Star
people.appearance: A short, thick man with a burnt beard and forearms speckled white with old spark scars, who listens to every blade he picks up before he looks at it.
people.backstory: Cát Lưu Quang was born among the sulphur gatherers at Xích Viêm Khẩu, the one fire vent in Ngọc Hành Sơn, and came up to the gate at twelve with a Fire root the mountain had not seen in a generation. The smiths' saying is that the mountain gives iron and the coal gives fire, and that a smith who is his own fire is born once a century. He was twenty when the gate bought the star that fell near Thanh Bách for three years of the city's taxes (A093). It lay unworked for seventy years, because no coal fire would soften it. In 1050 he became head and forged it in one winter by the Rite of the Fallen Star (A231), and named the blade for its price. He has two sons. The elder, Cát Đoán Nhạc (cat_doan_nhac), has no Fire. The younger, Cát Thối Phong (cat_thoi_phong), has it, and in 1170 Cát lent him to the Pivot as its armourer (N-thoi_tinh-02). In 1160 he broke the hammer of his best smith, Vưu Chước Kim (vuu_chuoc_kim), and sent him down the mountain for something Vưu said about the iron (N-thoi_tinh-01). He will not call Cát Thối Phong home for the Rite: the Pivot holds the loan, and the son wants the halberd under the barrow more than the forge. Since the spring he has taught the Rite to Đinh Hỏa Lân (dinh_hoa_lan) instead.
people.wants: To put the Rite of the Fallen Star into Đinh Hỏa Lân's hands before his own fail, so that the forge fire outlives him, and to keep his first son at the anvil while he does it.
people.secret: Vưu was right. The sky seam of Thiên Ngoại Khoáng gave out in 790 (N-thoi_tinh-04), before he was born; the mine has given mountain iron since, and only the Thanh Bách star sings. The gate has sold the mountain iron to the Pivot as star iron, at star-iron prices, for four centuries, and he still does.

people.appearance: His father's frame without the scars, in a black felt apron that never comes off.
people.backstory: Born at the gate and raised at the anvil by Cát Lưu Quang (cat_luu_quang), he is the best hammer on the mountain and he knows it. He forged the Plumb Line that the Pivot's head gave Công Tôn Duẫn (cong_ton_duan) in 1112, his finest work. He cannot hold the heat of the Rite of the Fallen Star. Since the spring his father has been teaching it to the Fire-born journeyman Đinh Hỏa Lân (dinh_hoa_lan) when the hammers stop. Cát Đoán Nhạc signs for the coal that comes up from Thạch Thán Khoáng, and he has cut the head's forge to a day's ration, so that the lessons burn the forge's winter store.

people.role: Quench-keeper of the snow-melt pool below the forge; holder of the founder's tongs
people.appearance: A thin old man with blue-white hands who stands knee-deep in the pool from dawn and never seems to feel it.
people.backstory: A coal-carrier's son from Thạch Thán Khoáng, with more Water in his root than a smith should have. Cát Lưu Quang (cat_luu_quang) gave him the founder's River Tongs, because by the founder's rule the one who strikes does not quench. He was standing in the pool in 1160 when Vưu Chước Kim (vuu_chuoc_kim) struck the ingots with lightning (N-thoi_tinh-01), and he never said what he heard. This autumn he named his price to the head: the pool and the tongs for Kha Ô Lan, or a sealed letter goes to Vưu.

people.role: Overseer of Thiên Ngoại Khoáng, the mine of the iron from beyond the sky
people.appearance: A broad, laughing woman with iron dust in her hair, who carries the mine's tally sticks in her belt.
people.backstory: A miner's daughter of Thiên Ngoại, she keeps the star mine and its two hundred diggers for Cát Lưu Quang (cat_luu_quang). She tells every buyer the ore fell with the stars (A222), and tells it well. She suspects what Vưu Chước Kim proved in 1160 and has decided it is not her business, as long as the Pivot's weighers at Song Kiều do not ask. She settles disputed tallies among her diggers by throwing dice, and the loser's share goes into the mine's purse.

people.role: Journeyman smith from Phất Y Cốc's steppe; the gate's best Fire root after the head, being taught the Rite
people.appearance: A lean, sun-dark man from the dry steppe who laughs at the snow and works the forge bare-chested in winter.
people.backstory: Born in Thập Giáp Thôn on the hot steppe below Phất Y Cốc, where Fire runs in the soil, he walked up the mountain at twenty to learn a trade and found that Cát Lưu Quang (cat_luu_quang) had been waiting for a fire like his for a century. He is Metal enough to pass the gate and no more. Since the spring the head has been teaching him the Rite of the Fallen Star in his own forge when the hammers stop, on less coal each month. Đinh talks aloud of taking the Rite home to the forges of Thập Giáp Thôn one day.

people.role: Founder of Thối Tinh Môn (330); the first to quench star iron in the mountain river
people.backstory: A miner of the high peaks who found iron that would not soften in a charcoal fire and believed it had fallen from the sky. He quenched it in the snow-melt river below the gate in 330 and founded the gate there (A221), then claimed the mine he called Thiên Ngoại (A222). He wrote the Star-Quench Canon and the rule that the one who strikes does not quench, and made the River Tongs for his quench-keeper.

people.role: Elder smith who forged the halberd Trầm Sa Kích for Quý Trường Kích in 600
people.backstory: The founder Diêu Lạc Tinh's (dieu_lac_tinh) last disciple. In 600 he forged the halberd Trầm Sa Kích from star iron for a young officer of the Pivot, Quý Trường Kích (quy_truong_kich) (C124), and visited him at the seat every decade to look at the edge. When the marshal fell on Chiết Kích Nguyên in 803 and was buried under the barrow with his halberd (C160), Nhạc asked to go and draw it, was refused, and stopped eating.

ties.note: the man he forged for
